sentences.en: Hello, and welcome to Speaking of Psychology, a podcast produced by the American Psychological
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听《心理学对话》，这是一个由美国心理学会

sentences.en: Association.
sentences.zh: 制作的播客。

sentences.en: I'm your host, Kim Mills, and I'm speaking to you from APA's Technology, Mind, and Society Conference in Washington.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人金·米尔斯，我在华盛顿的美国心理学会“技术、思维与社会”会议上为您进行采访。

sentences.en: This is an interdisciplinary meeting aimed at assessing current efforts to understand and shape the interactions of human beings and technology,
sentences.zh: 这是一场跨学科会议，旨在评估当前理解和塑造人类与技术互动的努力，

sentences.en: for identifying priorities for future work, and for promoting the exchange of ideas and collaboration among participants.
sentences.zh: 确定未来工作的重点，并促进与会者之间的思想交流与合作。

sentences.en: Dr. Christopher Ferguson is a professor of psychology at Stetson
sentences.zh: 克里斯托弗·弗格森博士是佛罗里达州德兰市斯特森

sentences.en: University in Deland, Florida.
sentences.zh: 大学的心理学教授。

sentences.en: He has clinical experience in working with offender and juvenile justice populations, as well as in conducting evaluations for child protective services.
sentences.zh: 他在与犯罪人员和少年司法群体打交道以及为儿童保护服务机构进行评估方面拥有临床经验。

sentences.en: His research focuses on media violence and video games in particular, and he recently served as guest editor
sentences.zh: 他的研究重点是媒体暴力，特别是电子游戏，他最近担任了

sentences.en: of a special issue of the APA Journal, Review of General Psychology, on that topic.
sentences.zh: 美国心理学会期刊《普通心理学评论》关于该主题特刊的客座主编。

sentences.en: But he's here today to talk about suicide contagion, which fits in with his interest in how political pressure, social panics,
sentences.zh: 但他今天来这里是为了讨论自杀传染，这符合他对政治压力、社会恐慌

sentences.en: and the so-called culture wars can distort media research.
sentences.zh: 以及所谓的文化战争如何扭曲媒体研究的兴趣。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Ferguson.
sentences.zh: 欢迎你，弗格森博士。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me here today.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来这里。

sentences.en: So the first question that comes to my mind is whether your research has shown that there is such a thing as suicide contagion.
sentences.zh: 那么我脑海中浮现的第一个问题是，您的研究是否表明存在自杀传染这种现象？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: So I mean, it really matters, contagion by who or what is really sort of an essential issue.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的很重要，被谁或什么传染确实是一个至关重要的问题。

sentences.en: So there really are sort of three pools of research on suicide contagion.
sentences.zh: 所以关于自杀传染的研究实际上大致可以分为三类。

sentences.en: One is by peers.
sentences.zh: 第一类是同龄人引起的。

sentences.en: So if one of your friends or someone in your social environment commits suicide, does that make you more likely to commit suicide, if you're kind of on that edge of considering it?
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你的一个朋友或你社交环境中的某个人自杀身亡，如果你正处于考虑自杀的边缘，这会让你更有可能自杀吗？

sentences.en: The second is by news media, so coverage of actual suicides in news media.
sentences.zh: 第二类是新闻媒体，也就是新闻媒体对真实自杀事件的报道。

sentences.en: And the third is with fictional television shows like 13 Reasons Why or even heavy metal music like Ozzy Osbourne and things like that.
sentences.zh: 第三类是虚构的电视剧，比如《十三个原因》，甚至是重金属音乐，比如奥兹·奥斯朋之类的事情。

sentences.en: And the research probably is pretty solid in terms of there being some sort of peer
sentences.zh: 就某种同龄人

sentences.en: contagion type of effect, that for individuals who are at risk for suicide, having a close associate commit suicide may elevate their risk somewhat.
sentences.zh: 传染效应而言，研究结果可能相当确凿，即对于有自杀风险的个人来说，有亲密伙伴自杀可能会在一定程度上提高他们的风险。

sentences.en: The news is a little bit, or news media effects are a little bit dodgier, but there seems to be some research they're suggesting there may or may not be
sentences.zh: 新闻的影响稍微，或者说新闻媒体的影响有点难以捉摸，但似乎有一些研究表明，当发生新闻媒体传染时，可能存在也可能

sentences.en: some effects when news media contagion.
sentences.zh: 不存在某些影响。

sentences.en: But I was really concerned with fictional media, sort of looking at shows like 13 Reasons Why and these kind of like fictional media portrayals of
sentences.zh: 但我真正关心的是虚构媒体，比如审视《十三个原因》这样的节目以及对自杀的这种虚构媒体刻画，

sentences.en: suicide and whether that would increase the likelihood of viewers committing suicide or thinking about suicide themselves.
sentences.zh: 并探讨这是否会增加观众自杀或自己考虑自杀的可能性。

sentences.en: And the literature has been going on for several decades, so I was kind of curious
sentences.zh: 相关文献已经存在了几十年，所以我很好奇

sentences.en: of summarizing that with a meta-analytic procedure, kind of looking at what are the overall trends in the research to date.
sentences.zh: 用元分析程序对这些进行总结，看看迄今为止研究的总体趋势是什么。

sentences.en: And although there's certainly some heterogeneity, there's some differences between studies in terms of whether effects seem to exist or not.
sentences.zh: 尽管肯定存在一些异质性，而且不同研究在效应是否存在方面也存在一些差异。

sentences.en: Overall, my analysis suggested that the data we have currently is probably not sufficient to support these kinds of concerns that we're having about shows like 13 Reasons Why.
sentences.zh: 总体而言，我的分析表明，我们目前拥有的数据可能不足以支持我们对《十三个原因》这类节目产生的种种担忧。

sentences.en: There does not seem to be a conclusive body of evidence to suggest that
sentences.zh: 似乎没有确凿的证据表明

sentences.en: suicide contagion happens through fictional media, at the very leaSt. So there was a lot of publicity last year
sentences.zh: 自杀传染会通过虚构媒体发生，至少可以说是这样。因此去年有很多公开宣传

sentences.en: around the article that was published by, I think it was the Journal of the American Medical Association,
sentences.zh: 围绕着一篇文章，我想是《美国医学会杂志》发表的，

sentences.en: we got that right, that saw a big spike around the time of the broadcaSt. And what they found was a lot of people doing internet searches for suicide.
sentences.zh: 我们没记错的话，它发现在节目播出期间出现了一个巨大的高峰。他们发现很多人在互联网上搜索有关自杀的信息。

sentences.en: Was that not a good piece of research?
sentences.zh: 那难道不是一项好的研究吗？

sentences.en: It's not so much that it wasn't a good piece of research.
sentences.zh: 与其说它不是一项好的研究，

sentences.en: It's more that, it wasn't clear from those searches whether those individuals who were doing those searches were intending to commit suicide,
sentences.zh: 不如说，从这些搜索中并不清楚那些进行搜索的人是否必然打算自杀，

sentences.en: necessarily, or if they were just curious about the topic, or even may have been seeking help because they had been thinking about suicide previously.
sentences.zh: 或者他们只是对这个话题感到好奇，甚至可能是因为之前考虑过自杀而一直在寻求帮助。

sentences.en: So it wasn't really sure that those searches translated into real behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以并不确定这些搜索是否转化为了实际行为。

sentences.en: And the example might be is that, you know, in all likelihood after, of course, we've had a lot of news recently about, you know, gun violence and
sentences.zh: 一个例子可能是，你知道，毫无疑问，在最近我们有了很多关于枪支暴力和

sentences.en: tragic shootings, that it's very likely that after a tragic shooting occurs, you see a lot more searches about gun violence, mass shootings, so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 悲惨枪击事件的新闻之后，很有可能在悲惨枪击事件发生后，你会看到更多关于枪支暴力、大规模枪击事件等方面的搜索。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that the majority of those individuals are, you know, likely to go out and commit those shootings as well.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着这些人的绝大多数，你知道，也很可能会出去实施这些枪击事件。

sentences.en: So it seems to be the same sort of an issue.
sentences.zh: 所以这似乎是同一种问题。

sentences.en: People were doing a lot more searches about suicide and suicide related issues.
sentences.zh: 人们对自杀及自杀相关问题的搜索增多了。

sentences.en: But it doesn't seem to be that that was an indication that those individuals were inclined to
sentences.zh: 但这似乎并不能表明这些人倾向于

sentences.en: actually engage in suicide, or that that translated into an increased risk of suicide behaviors among viewers.
sentences.zh: 真正实施自杀，或者这转化为观众自杀行为风险的增加。

sentences.en: Did you look at all into the kinds of messages that the producers are putting on the program now to kind of warn people?
sentences.zh: 你是否研究过制作人在节目中加入的用来提醒人们的那类信息？

sentences.en: I mean, you know, there's some concern about triggering, does it help if there's some message at the beginning of the program or at the end of the program for resources?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，人们对触发因素有些担忧，如果节目开始或结束时有提供求助资源的提示信息，会有帮助吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, they can be helpful for people who are maybe offended by content, you know, so to sort of warn people of what's coming, so that they're not surprised by it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，对于那些可能被内容冒犯的人来说，这些信息可能会有帮助，你知道的，也就是提醒人们即将发生什么，这样他们就不会对此感到惊讶。

sentences.en: I think at this point, they're probably relatively few people who would learn that 13 Reasons Why is about suicide.
sentences.zh: 我想在这一点上，可能相对很少有人不知道《十三个原因》是关于自杀的。

sentences.en: So it's probably not, you know, in that sense, it's probably not a huge deal.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种意义上，这可能不是什么大不了的事。

sentences.en: I mean, it's always good to have people be informed in terms of whether they want to decide if they want to be exposed to a particular content issue or not.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，让人们了解情况总是好的，这样他们就可以决定自己是否愿意接触某个特定的内容问题。

sentences.en: But in terms of, you know, sort of trigger warnings, as you mentioned, being sort of a fix for possible effects, there actually was some
sentences.zh: 但就你提到的触发警告而言，作为可能产生影响的补救措施，实际上有一些

sentences.en: research that I had come across at a conference a year or two ago that actually suggested that oftentimes trigger
sentences.zh: 我在一两年前的一次会议上接触到的研究实际上表明，通常触发

sentences.en: warnings can actually increase people's anxiety about content, so have kind of a paradoxical effect.
sentences.zh: 警告实际上会增加人们对内容的焦虑，从而产生某种悖论效应。

sentences.en: And they weren't looking at suicide-themed media, they were looking more like even like Shakespeare novels and, you know, sexual content, violent content.
sentences.zh: 他们研究的不是以自杀为主题的媒体，而是更像莎士比亚小说、性内容、暴力内容之类的主题。

sentences.en: But that oftentimes if, you know, if you just sort of expose people to something, they don't think it's necessarily a huge deal.
sentences.zh: 但通常情况下，如果你只是让人们接触某些东西，他们不一定认为这是一件大事。

sentences.en: But if you warn them about it in advance, then they actually are sort of primed to worry about it and they actually have a bit more of a written emotional reaction
sentences.zh: 但如果你提前警告他们，那么他们实际上就会倾向于为此担忧，并且与你某种程度上顺其自然相比，他们实际上会对此产生更多的书面情绪反应

sentences.en: to it than if you had just left it alone to some extent.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这比你任由它不管还要好一些。

sentences.en: It kind of depends on what the content is probably.
sentences.zh: 这可能在很大程度上取决于具体内容是什么。

sentences.en: If it's super shocking, the trigger warning might help.
sentences.zh: 如果内容超级震撼，触发警告可能会有帮助。

sentences.en: If it's maybe not so shocking, then it might actually be kind of paradoxical in terms of its effect.
sentences.zh: 如果可能没有那么震撼，那么它的效果实际上可能有点矛盾。

sentences.en: Did you look at contagion in other realms?
sentences.zh: 你有没有研究过其他领域的传染现象？

sentences.en: I mean, there's a lot of writing research around, oh, I don't know, school shootings, for example, and whether those happen to be contagious or even fashion trends or, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有很多关于，哦，我不知道，例如校园枪击案的研究，关于这些事件是否具有传染性，甚至时尚潮流，或者，你知道的，

sentences.en: things that people do with the stock market, for example.
sentences.zh: 人们在股市中所做的事情，等等。

sentences.en: Right, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，是的。

sentences.en: Well, this study was limited just to the fictional media suicide contagion issues.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这项研究仅限于虚构媒体的自杀传染问题。

sentences.en: Of course, there is a lot of discussion, you know, with these tragic shootings about the issue of gun violence
sentences.zh: 当然，随着这些悲惨的枪击事件，关于枪支暴力的议题有大量的讨论，

sentences.en: and the possibility that news media coverage of school shootings or mass shootings may actually serve as a motivating factor
sentences.zh: 并且新闻媒体对校园枪击或大规模枪击事件的报道实际上可能成为其中一些枪手的激励因素。

sentences.en: for some of these shooters.
sentences.zh: 事实上，并没有太多关于这方面的非常好的数据。

sentences.en: Actually, it's not a lot of really good data on that.
sentences.zh: 因此，目前已经有很多研究在探讨枪支暴力的频率在新闻报道之后是增加还是减少。

sentences.en: So there have now been a lot of studies looking at whether the frequency of gun violence increases or decreases after news coverage.
sentences.zh: 所以其中很多研究仍然非常具有推测性。

sentences.en: So a lot of that still is very speculative.
sentences.zh: 其中一些或许基于这样一种错误印象，即大多数大规模枪击案制造者都是为了引起注意。

sentences.en: Some of that is perhaps based on a misimpression that the majority of mass shooters are out for attention.
sentences.zh: 有些人似乎确实如此。

sentences.en: Some appear to be.
sentences.zh: 因此，当然有一些例子，比如桑迪胡克小学枪击案的枪手或弗吉尼亚理工大学枪击案的枪手，他们都曾提及科伦拜恩枪击案，例如。

sentences.en: So there have certainly been examples of like the Sandy Hook shooter or the Virginia Tech shooter who referred back to Columbine, for instance.
sentences.zh: 所以某些枪手之间似乎至少有时存在某种认同效应。

sentences.en: So there seems to be sometime at least some identification effect between some shooters.
sentences.zh: 但你并不一定在所有人身上都能看到这一点，甚至不一定在绝大多数人身上看到。

sentences.en: But you don't necessarily see that with all of them or even necessarily the majority.
sentences.zh: 所以我不敢确定，例如，采取诸如不使用枪手名字之类的措施一定会对枪支暴力或大规模枪击事件产生重大影响。

sentences.en: So I'm not sure that, for instance, taking steps like not using shooters' names is necessarily going to have a big effect on gun violence or mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，避免使用枪手名字也没有什么坏处。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, there isn't really any harm either in avoiding using shooters' names.
sentences.zh: 所以既然没有坏处，我想不妨就这么做吧。

sentences.en: So if there's no harm, might as well do it, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 你知道，以防万一，那里可能存在一些微小的影响。

sentences.en: You know, on the off chance, maybe there's some small effect there.
sentences.zh: 但它可能不是解决枪支暴力或大规模枪击等问题的关键所在。

sentences.en: But it's probably not going to be the main thing that solves issues like gun violence or mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 那么社会传染研究的下一步计划是什么？

sentences.en: So what are the next steps in terms of research for the social contagion?
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们需要，你知道的，更好、更透明和开放科学的研究。

sentences.en: Well, we need, you know, a lot better, more transparent and open science research.
sentences.zh: 所以这一直是整个媒体研究中的一个常见主题，包括暴力电子游戏研究、身体形象研究和其他领域，

sentences.en: So this has been kind of a common theme in media research in general, including violent video game research and body image research and other fields that
sentences.zh: 过去进行的许多研究并不是非常透明。

sentences.en: a lot of the research that have been done in the past was not very transparent.
sentences.zh: 当人们来尝试重复其中的一些研究时，有些研究的复现效果并不好。

sentences.en: Some of it isn't replicating very well when people are coming and trying to replicate some of those studies.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们在大约15年前或20年前认为绝对真实的很多事情，现在证明非常难以复现。

sentences.en: So a lot of things that we thought were sort of absolutely true maybe 15 years ago or 20 years ago are now proving very difficult to replicate.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们这个领域以及其他与媒体相关的领域非常需要大量真正扎实、设计良好、预注册、透明、开放科学的研究。

sentences.en: So we're really in need in this field and in other media-related fields for a lot of really solid, well-designed, pre-registered, transparent, open science research.
sentences.zh: 这也是我在此领域进行的这项元分析中发现的有趣事情之一，你知道的，

sentences.en: And that was one of the interesting things with this meta-analysis I conducted with this field is that, you know,
sentences.zh: 很多研究都还可以，但存在很多常见问题。

sentences.en: a lot of the studies were okay, but there were a lot of common issues.
sentences.zh: 就像许多调查设计一样，它们会询问孩子们观看的电视节目，然后询问他们对自杀的感受，你知道的，你有没有在考虑自杀？

sentences.en: Like with a lot of the survey designs, they would ask about TV shows kids would watch and then ask them how they felt about suicide, you know, are you thinking about suicide?
sentences.zh: 要猜出该研究的假设并不是那么难。

sentences.en: It's not that hard to guess the hypothesis of that study.
sentences.zh: 有时这会以这样或那样的方式改变人们的行为。

sentences.en: And sometimes that can change people's behavior one way or another.
sentences.zh: 因此，看到更多试图摆脱这种模式的研究将会非常好，

sentences.en: So it would be really good to see a lot more studies that are trying to get away from that,
sentences.zh: 更好地掩盖假设，对人们进行更长时间的追踪，以了解长期的影响是什么。

sentences.en: masking the hypothesis better, following people over longer periods of time to see what the long-term effects are.
sentences.zh: 我认为这将有助于阐明这些类型的效应在这个领域中是否存在。

sentences.en: And I think that would help elucidate whether these types of effects do or do not exist in this field.
sentences.zh: 所以我们实际上正在斯特森大学做一些这方面的工作，我们刚刚开始一项关于青少年及其观看习惯

sentences.en: So we're actually trying to do a little bit of that at Stetson University and we're just now starting a longitudinal study of youth and their viewing habits
sentences.zh: 与情绪相关问题（包括自杀）的纵向研究。

sentences.en: and mood-related issues including suicide.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 我很期待看到你的研究发表。

sentences.en: I look forward to seeing that when you get it published.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: Same here.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢弗格森博士今天加入我们的节目。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Well, thank you very much, Dr. Ferguson, for joining us today.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for having me on.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 感谢您加入我们的播客。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure.
